problem: Indoor robots' navigation policies, including navigation VLAs, use only on-board views and ignore existing infrastructure (CCTV) cameras that see hidden objects and blocked aisles; naively adding a CCTV encoder does not make the policy use it because CCTV-dependent decision points are rare (shortcut learning / copycat).
motivation: Warehouses, hospitals and offices already have cameras showing the current state in real time, unlike stale maps. An end-to-end VLA can learn what to take from such views, but behavior cloning lets the policy reach low loss by ignoring them, so a training recipe that creates an incentive to use them is needed.
key_idea: Add a dedicated, pooled CCTV encoder producing tokens to a pretrained navigation VLA (OmniVLA), and train in two stages: counterfactual-snippet upsampling, then HG-DAgger-style recovery data mined within snippets to force reliance on the CCTV views.
insight: Architecture alone fails: CCTV without upsampling gives 36.0% SR (vs 34.0% baseline) on the semantic task, and upsampling lifts it to 100%. In the spatial task, upsampling alone yields a copycat shortcut (route match 44.4%), and recovery data breaks the heading-to-route correlation (100% SR, 91.7-95.8% shortest route). Ablations show detail must be preserved (16 tokens per view: 28.0% SR) and that the LLM/on-board encoder must be fine-tuned (frozen: 26-90%).
method: CCTV encoder: a dedicated per-view encoder (initialized from the on-board encoder and projector, DINOv2+SigLIP features) whose tokens are inserted after the on-board and goal-image tokens, keeping OmniVLA's pretrained positions.
Token pooling: 2x2 average pooling reduces 256 to 64 tokens per view so several cameras fit in the LLaMA-2 7B context.
Fine-tuning: LoRA (rank 16) on all linear layers; the language-following loss is dropped; the loss is waypoint MSE plus a smoothness term (lambda=0.1), predicting H=8 waypoints (x, y, cos, sin).

Stage 1, counterfactual snippets: pairs of demonstrations from the same start with different instruction or scene are used; windows around the split are extracted and upsampled to ~50% of sampling mass to raise I(A;Z|X).

Stage 2, recovery data: roll out the stage-1 policy inside snippets; when it exceeds distance d_r=0.5 m from the demonstrated path, an A* supervisor returns it and only the return segment is kept (K trajectories); training continues on a mix of recovery data and CF snippets.
Execution: the fifth predicted waypoint is converted to velocities via the inverse unicycle model, at 3 Hz.

setting.backbone: OmniVLA (OpenVLA-derived, LLaMA-2 7B with DINOv2+SigLIP encoders), LoRA fine-tuned, plus a new CCTV encoder
setting.training_data: Task-specific demos: semantic sim 552 train trajectories (3.03 h); spatial sim 481 trajectories (6.89 h); real Spot 75 trajectories (~10 min, 0.16 h); plus recovery data (K up to 48) in simulation; starts from the OmniVLA checkpoint at 120k steps
setting.observation: On-board monocular RGB plus N fixed static CCTV RGB views (4 in sim, 2 real); the camera parameters are not provided to the policy
setting.action_space: 8 predicted waypoints (x, y, cos, sin) converted to forward/angular velocity
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (warehouse, Nova Carter) plus a real Boston Dynamics Spot
setting.privileged: none at test time (A* oracle supervisor only for training data; a human operator judges real-world success)

numbers.extra: 4 CCTV cameras; 50 rollouts; single training run
separate policy with 2 of 9 patterns held out

numbers.eval_set_note: 34 rollouts, forklift in the held-out aisle
numbers.extra: separate policy trained with these scenes held out
fine-tuned on 75 teleoperated trajectories (<10 min); 2 CCTV; human-judged success

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks only (no standard public benchmark). All results come from a single training run.
results: InfraVLA reaches 100% SR on both simulated tasks, versus 34.0% (semantic) and 73.6% (spatial) for the fine-tuned no-CCTV OmniVLA baseline; on the spatial task 95.8% of rollouts take the shortest route (K=24) versus 55.6% for the baseline. OOD SR is 88.2% and 88.9%, and the real Spot reaches 83.3% versus 29.2% for the baseline.
limitations: Single training run per result, no seeds or statistics; one facility, at most 4 cameras, and fixed start poses in the language tasks
Inference time doubles (95 to 190 ms with 4 views) and grows with camera count
Stage 2 recovery is untested on the real robot; the real-world evaluation is small (24 rollouts, operator-judged)
